newsitem.title: USA: Two Calif. counties added to flood emergency list.
newsitem.headline: Two Calif. counties added to flood emergency list.

text.p: A top California state official has declared a state of emergency in the city and county of San Francisco and in Alameda County due to flood damage from recent winter storms, his office said on Monday.

"This proclamation orders the use of state personnel, equipment and facilities to alleviate the emergency, and will make it easier for the two counties to qualify for state and federal disaster assistance," acting Gov. Bill Lockyer said.
Recent floods caused at least $3.5 million in damage to property owned by San Francisco and its residents. San Francisco streets, sewer lines and the port sustained damage.
In Alameda County, more than 150 homes and businesses were damaged, along with roads and flood control systems.
With San Francisco and Alameda added to the emergency list, a total of 46 of California's 58 counties are now under state of emergency declarations, state officials said.

Lockyer, president pro tem of the state Senate, assumed the role of acting governor because both Gov. Pete Wilson and Lt. Gov. Gray Davis were out of the state. Wilson is traveling in Asia and Davis is in Washington.
According to state officials, damage estimates from the devastating New Year floods have passed $1.5 billion.
